$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-countries.mjs — do not edit by hand.
source: CLDR region data bundled with Node's ICU (no network, no npm dependency)

notAssigned.AC: Exceptionally reserved (Ascension Island). Residents use SH — St Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha.
notAssigned.TA: Exceptionally reserved (Tristan da Cunha). Residents use SH.
notAssigned.CP: Exceptionally reserved (Clipperton Island). Uninhabited; sovereignty FR.
notAssigned.DG: Exceptionally reserved (Diego Garcia). Falls under IO.
notAssigned.EA: Exceptionally reserved (Ceuta & Melilla). Residents use ES.
notAssigned.IC: Exceptionally reserved (Canary Islands). Residents use ES.
notAssigned.CQ: Exceptionally reserved for Sark (2019). Sark is in the Bailiwick of Guernsey; residents use GG.
notAssigned.ZZ: CLDR sentinel for an unknown region. Never a real answer to "where do you drive?".
notAssigned.XK: User-assigned (Kosovo). No ISO 3166-1 code exists — see EXCEPTIONS.
notAssigned.EU: Exceptionally reserved (European Union). Supranational, not a country.
notAssigned.EZ: Exceptionally reserved (Eurozone). Supranational, not a country.
notAssigned.UN: Exceptionally reserved (United Nations). An organisation, not a country.
notAssigned.QO: CLDR macroregion (Outlying Oceania). Not an ISO 3166-1 code at all.
notAssigned.XA: ICU pseudo-locale for accent testing. Not a place. Ships in ICU's region data.
notAssigned.XB: ICU pseudo-locale for bidi testing. Not a place.

exceptions.XK: Kosovo. ~1.8M people and no ISO 3166-1 code exists, so unlike every other entry in NOT_ASSIGNED there is no correct fallback: the nearest code is RS, which is factually wrong and, on an app with public national leaderboards, gratuitously so. XK sits in the XA–XZ range that ISO 3166-1 reserves for user assignment, so shipping it is conformant with the standard rather than a deviation from it, and it is what the EU, IMF, World Bank and Unicode all use in practice.
